<result># `intropy deploy` / `intropy release` — Information Inventory

## 1. Command surface

Both roots are registered in `cmd/intropy`. There is **no** `internal/cli/*`; commands are flat files in `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/cmd/intropy/` and logic lives in `/Users/robinhultman/dev/intropy/tooling/intropy-cli/internal/deploy/` and `/internal/release/`.

| Command | Definition | Args |
|---|---|---|
| `deploy <component> [version]` | `cmd/intropy/deploy.go:29` | 1–2 |
| `deploy init [component...]` | `cmd/intropy/deploy_init.go:33` | arbitrary |
| `deploy promote <component>` | `cmd/intropy/deploy_promote.go:29` | 1 |
| `deploy diff <component>` | `cmd/intropy/deploy_diff.go:23` | 1 |
| `deploy sync <component>` | `cmd/intropy/deploy_sync.go:28` | 1 |
| `deploy status <component>` | `cmd/intropy/deploy_status.go:22` | 1 |
| `release create <component>` | `cmd/intropy/release_create.go:25` | 1 |
| `release view <component> <version>` | `cmd/intropy/release_view.go:21` | 2 |

Flags (from the `init()` blocks):

- **`deploy`** (`deploy.go:145-165`): `--env/-e` (required), `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--plan`, `--allow-dirty`, `--no-wait`, `--timeout`, `--output/-o` (plain|json).
- **`deploy init`** (`deploy_init.go:146-163`): `--domain`, `--system`, `--env/-e` (slice), `--topology`, `--source-dir`, `--version` (template release tag), `--values/-f`, `--set/-s`, `--no-input`, `--plan`, `--force`, `--gitops-repo`, `--output/-o`. Deliberately no `--argocd-server`/`--no-wait`/`--timeout`/`--allow-dirty` (`deploy_init.go:166-169`).
- **`deploy promote`** (`deploy_promote.go:88-98`): `--from` (req), `--to` (req), `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--plan`, `--no-wait`, `--timeout`, `--output`.
- **`deploy diff`** (`deploy_diff.go:69-75`): `--env` (req), `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--output`.
- **`deploy sync`** (`deploy_sync.go:73-82`): `--env` (req), `--revision`, `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--no-wait`, `--timeout`, `--output`.
- **`deploy status`** (`deploy_status.go:64-69`): `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--argocd-server`, `--output`. Deliberately no `--env`.
- **`release create`** (`release_create.go:68-76`): `--version` (req), `--ref`, `--since`, `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--allow-dirty`, `--output`.
- **`release view`** (`release_view.go:52-56`): `--domain`, `--system`, `--gitops-repo`, `--output`.

Shell completions read the **cached GitOps checkout** offline (`deploy.go:116-138`, `release.go:20-36`) — component names, domains, and `deploy.yaml` environment names are therefore locally enumerable without network access.

---

## 2. The release record (`release create` / `release view`)

### Storage location

**Not** a local file and **not** the gitops repo. It is a tag-addressed **OCI artifact** in the same registry as the images, in a sibling repository:

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:30
const ReleasesRepoSuffix = "/releases"
// :43
func ReleasesRepo(image string) string {
	return strings.TrimSuffix(image, "/") + ReleasesRepoSuffix
}
// :48
func Ref(releasesRepo, version string) string { return releasesRepo + ":" + version }
```

The repo is derived from `component.yaml`'s `images[0].name` (`internal/release/create.go:102`), so e.g. `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/order-extractor/releases:1.4.2`. Media types (immutable by design):

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:16-18
ArtifactType  = "application/vnd.integrio.release.v1"
MediaTypeJSON = "application/vnd.integrio.release.v1+json"
```

### The manifest itself

```go
// internal/release/manifest.go:22
const SchemaVersion = 1

// internal/release/manifest.go:29-40
type Manifest struct {
	SchemaVersion int         `json:"schemaVersion"`
	Component     string      `json:"component"`
	Version       string      `json:"version"`
	CreatedAt     time.Time   `json:"createdAt"`
	CreatedBy     string      `json:"createdBy"`
	Source        Source      `json:"source"`
	Images        []Image     `json:"images"`
	Notes         string      `json:"notes"`
	Changes       []Change    `json:"changes"`
	ChangeBasis   ChangeBasis `json:"changeBasis"`
}

// :43-47
type Source struct {
	Commit string `json:"commit"`
	Ref    string `json:"ref"`
	Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"`
}

// :54-57
type Image struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Digest string `json:"digest"`
}

// :60-63
type Change struct {
	Commit  string `json:"commit"`
	Subject string `json:"subject"`
}

// :84-93
type ChangeBasis struct {
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Version and Commit identify the predecessor when Kind is BasisRelease.
	Version string `json:"version,omitempty"`
	Commit  string `json:"commit,omitempty"`
	// Ref is what the operator passed to --since when Kind is BasisExplicit.
	Ref string `json:"ref,omitempty"`
}
```

`ChangeBasis.Kind` ∈ `{"initial","release","explicit"}` (`manifest.go:70-76`). Note **`Source.Repo` is the GitOps repository URL, not the source repo** — `create.go:137` sets `Source{Commit: commit, Ref: opts.Ref, Repo: repoURL}` where `repoURL` came from `RequireGitopsRepo()`. That URL frequently encodes the customer (`git@gitlab.com:integrio/intropy/customers/acme/gitops.git`, README:784) and is therefore embedded in every published release manifest.

`CreatedBy` is scraped from the environment:

```go
// internal/release/create.go:292-299
func committer() string {
	for _, key := range []string{"GITLAB_USER_EMAIL", "GITHUB_ACTOR", "USER"} {
		if v := os.Getenv(key); v != "" { return v }
	}
	return ""
}
```

(An identical `committer()` exists at `internal/deploy/publish.go:232`.) So an operator email/username lands in both the release manifest and every deploy commit.

### OCI annotations (visible in a registry UI without pulling the layer)

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:79-87
Annotations: map[string]string{
	AnnotationComponent:                    m.Component,        // io.intropy.release.component
	AnnotationCommit:                       m.Source.Commit,    // io.intropy.release.source-commit
	"org.opencontainers.image.title":       m.Component,
	"org.opencontainers.image.version":     m.Version,
	"org.opencontainers.image.created":     m.CreatedAt.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z"),
	"org.opencontainers.image.revision":    m.Source.Commit,
	"org.opencontainers.image.description": firstLine(m.Notes),
},
```

`firstLine(m.Notes)` is the **first commit subject** of the changelog, promoted into a registry annotation.

### Ancestry / changelog derivation

`PreviousRelease` (`internal/release/changelog.go:44`) lists *all* tags in the releases repo (`ListVersions` → `reg.ListTags`), pulls each manifest, and picks the nearest ancestor by `git merge-base --is-ancestor` rather than version sort. Consequences for information flow: creating one release **reads every other release manifest of that component**, and `Changes` is `git log <prev>..<commit> -- <sourcePaths>` (`changelog.go:108-119`) — i.e. **commit SHAs + subjects scoped to the component's `sourcePaths`** are copied verbatim into the manifest and into `Notes` as `- <subject>` lines (`RenderNotes`, `changelog.go:122`).

### Git tag side-effect

```go
// internal/release/create.go:244-246
func TagName(component, version string) string { return component + "/v" + version }
// :280-282  annotated tag message
func tagMessage(m *Manifest) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\n\n%s", m.Component, m.Version, m.Notes)
}
```

Pushed to `origin` in the **source** repo. Failure is a warning only (`create.go:271-275`).

### `release create` machine-readable result

```go
// internal/release/request.go:84-101
type Result struct {
	Component string `json:"component"`
	Version   string `json:"version"`
	Ref       string `json:"ref"`      // full OCI ref
	Digest    string `json:"digest"`   // manifest digest
	Created   bool   `json:"created"`
	Tag       string `json:"tag"`
	Tagged    bool   `json:"tagged"`
	Manifest  *Manifest `json:"manifest"`
}
```

`release view -o json` emits the raw `Manifest` (`internal/release/view.go:73-77`).

---

## 3. `deploy init` — what gets scaffolded and recorded

### Where it writes

- Renders into a **temp staging dir** `os.MkdirTemp("", "intropy-deploy-init-*")` mirroring the repo root (`init.go:182`).
- Writes into the cached GitOps checkout and pushes a **branch, never the default branch**:
  ```go
  // internal/deploy/init.go:39
  const initBranchPrefix = "deploy-init/"
  // :192
  branch := initBranchPrefix + facts.Domain + "-" + facts.System
  ```
- Tree shape: `domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/…` plus a shared host dir:
  ```go
  // internal/deploy/init.go:36
  const HostDirName = "host"
  ```
- Two templates, fetched from the **external** library `integrio-intropy/intropy-templates` (`internal/template/github.go:14-15`):
  ```go
  // internal/deploy/init.go:26-27
  TemplateDeployHost      = "deploy-host"
  TemplateDeployComponent = "deploy-component"
  ```

The actual manifest bodies live in that other repo. The in-repo fixtures at `internal/deploy/init_test.go:20-175` mirror the real shape and show exactly what is generated: `component.yaml`, `base/dapr/pubsub-rabbitmq.yaml` **or** `pubsub-servicebus.yaml` (a `dapr.io/v1alpha1 Component` with `spec.metadata.connectionString.secretKeyRef` and a `scopes:` list built from the topology app-ids), `base/secrets/secrets.yaml` (a `v1 Secret` with `stringData: rabbitmq-connection: REPLACE-ME-RABBITMQ-CONNECTION-STRING`), `base/cronjob.yaml` (`batch/v1 CronJob`, `schedule: "REPLACE-ME-CRON-SCHEDULE"`) or `base/deployment.yaml`, and `overlays/<env>/kustomization.yaml` (carrying `namespace:`).

The cronjob-vs-deployment decision is derived, not asked:

```go
// internal/deploy/initmodel.go:22-25
WorkloadCronJob    = "cronjob"
WorkloadDeployment = "deployment"
// :235-240
func workloadFor(kind string) string {
	if strings.EqualFold(kind, blockKindExtractor) { return WorkloadCronJob }
	return WorkloadDeployment
}
```

### The information handed to templates

Three reserved injections plus seeds. Seeds (`init.go:743-772`):

```go
seeds := map[string]any{
	"domain": facts.Domain, "system": facts.System, "hostName": HostDirName,
	"registry": facts.Registry, "argocdAppNamespace": facts.AppNamespace,
	"provider": facts.Platform.Provider, "pubsub": facts.Platform.Pubsub,
	"secretStore": facts.Platform.SecretStore,
}
// + pubsubName when unambiguous; + name/kind/appId/workload/sourceDir per component
```

Reserved `.gitops` map (`init.go:796-812`): `domain, system, component, env, host, registry, argocdAppNamespace, environments[], platform{provider,pubsub,secretStore}`.

Reserved `.scaffold` = the component's **entire `.intropy/scaffold.json` `values` map** (`init.go:816-821`) — i.e. whatever `int create` recorded is available to any manifest template.

Reserved `.topology` = the derived model, fully sorted for byte-identical re-renders:

```go
// internal/deploy/initmodel.go:40-46
type InitModel struct {
	System     string          `json:"system"`
	Components []InitComponent `json:"components"`
	PubSubs    []InitPubSub    `json:"pubsubs"`
	Topics     []InitTopic     `json:"topics"`
	Connectors []InitConnector `json:"connectors"`
}
// :49-72
type InitComponent struct {
	Name string `json:"name"`; Kind string `json:"kind"`
	AppID string `json:"appId"`; Workload string `json:"workload"`
	Dir string `json:"dir,omitempty"`
	Topics []string `json:"topics,omitempty"`; Connectors []string `json:"connectors,omitempty"`
}
// :75-82
type InitPubSub struct { Name string; Topics []string; AppIDs []string }  // appIds → Dapr scopes
// :85-91
type InitTopic struct { PubSub, Topic, Contract string; Publishers, Subscribers []string }
// :96-102
type InitConnector struct { Name, ExternalSystem, Transport string; Directions, AppIDs []string }
```

Upstream source of that model is the .NET host's `graph` verb (`internal/topology/graph.go:28`, `dotnet run … -- graph`), decoded into `topology.Topology` (`internal/topology/topology.go:33-128`): `apiVersion/kind/system/components[]/topics[]/connectors[]/contracts[]/apis[]`, where `Contract` carries `name, kind, shortName, mediaType, fingerprint, schema (raw JSON Schema)`. The full record can also be supplied via `--topology file|-`. Note the CLI's own model **drops** contracts/schemas — only `InitTopic.Contract` (the FQ type name) survives into templates.

### Record file? — No dedicated one, but there is a commit + a result document

`deploy init` writes **no** `.intropy/*.json`. Its durable record is the branch commit:

```go
// internal/deploy/init.go:905-907
func scaffoldSubject(facts initFacts, files int) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("deploy-init(%s): scaffold %d file%s under %s", facts.System, files, plural(files), facts.Domain)
}
// :909-929  trailers: Deploy-Domain, Deploy-System, Deploy-Component (one per selected), Deploy-By, Deploy-Cli
```

And the stdout result:

```go
// internal/deploy/result.go:136-159
type InitResult struct {
	System string `json:"system"`
	Domain string `json:"domain"`
	Host   string `json:"host"`
	Template string `json:"template"`       // "owner/repo@tag" — internal/template/library.go:104
	Components []string `json:"components"`
	Files []FileAction `json:"files"`
	Applied  bool   `json:"applied"`
	Branch   string `json:"branch,omitempty"`
	Revision string `json:"revision,omitempty"`
	Placeholders []Placeholder `json:"placeholders"`
}
// scaffold.go:35-39
type FileAction struct {
	Rel    string `json:"path"`
	Action string `json:"action"`   // create | identical | skip-exists | overwrite
}
// placeholder.go:29-37
type Placeholder struct {
	File  string `json:"file"`
	Line  int    `json:"line"`
	Token string `json:"token"`
}
```

`Placeholder` is the notable one for exposure analysis: it is a **greppable index of every un-filled secret slot** in the generated tree, discovered by

```go
// internal/deploy/placeholder.go:22
const PlaceholderPrefix = "REPLACE-ME-"
// :26
var placeholderPattern = regexp.MustCompile(`REPLACE-ME-[A-Z0-9-]*[A-Z0-9]`)
```

with hints like `REPLACE-ME-RABBITMQ-CONNECTION-STRING`, `REPLACE-ME-SFTP-HOST`, `REPLACE-ME-CRON-SCHEDULE`. Image tags are deliberately excluded (`placeholder.go:46-48`). `--force` is refused when it would overwrite an overlay pinning a digest (`scaffold.go:117-141`).

---

## 4. What `deploy`/`promote` write into git

### The overlay edit

Two `commonAnnotations` plus `images[]` digest pins:

```go
// internal/kustomize/editor.go:22
const AnnotationSourceCommit = "deploy.internal/source-commit"
// :31
const AnnotationRelease = "deploy.internal/release"
```

Applied by `applyEdits` (`internal/deploy/plan.go:250-271`); the release annotation is **removed** on a commit-based deploy so a stale version can't mislead `promote`.

### Commit trailers (a documented, read-back format)

```go
// internal/deploy/publish.go:19-41
TrailerComponent   = "Deploy-Component"
TrailerDomain      = "Deploy-Domain"
TrailerSystem      = "Deploy-System"
TrailerEnvironment = "Deploy-Env"
TrailerRelease     = "Deploy-Release"
TrailerPromotedFrom = "Deploy-Promoted-From"
TrailerImage        = "Deploy-Image"
TrailerDigest       = "Deploy-Digest"
TrailerSourceCommit = "Deploy-Source-Commit"
TrailerBy           = "Deploy-By"
TrailerCli          = "Deploy-Cli"
```

Built in `commitTrailers` (`publish.go:191-227`) — one `Deploy-Image`/`Deploy-Digest` pair per pin. Subjects are built in `commitSubject` (`publish.go:160-179`). Read back by `pendingProvenance` (`internal/deploy/diff.go:197-227`) into:

```go
// internal/deploy/diff.go:164-170
type provenance struct { Subject, Release, PromotedFrom, SourceCommit, By string }
```

so `deploy diff` surfaces **who deployed what, from where** to an approver — and into `DiffResult.DeployedBy`.

### Internal intermediate structures

```go
// internal/deploy/plan.go:17-68
type Plan struct {
	Coordinate gitops.Coordinate; Environment string; Source source.State
	ReleaseVersion string; PromotedFrom string
	Pins []source.Pin; Previous map[string]string; PreviousRelease string
	Upstreams []Upstream; Notes []string
	Diff string; DigestChanged bool
	OverlayDir string; KustomizationPath string
}
// internal/deploy/snapshot.go:20-35  (what promote copies)
type snapshot struct { Environment string; Pins []source.Pin; Commit, Release, Revision string }
// internal/deploy/upstream.go:32-44
type Upstream struct {
	Environment string `json:"environment"`
	Status      string `json:"status"`           // match|differs|unpinned|unknown
	Pinned      map[string]string `json:"pinned,omitempty"`
	SourceCommit string `json:"sourceCommit,omitempty"`
}
// internal/source/digest.go:21-30
type Pin struct { Image, Digest, Tag string }
// internal/source/source.go:20-30
type State struct { Commit, Branch string; Dirty []string }   // Dirty = list of dirty paths
```

`State.Dirty` holds **paths of uncommitted files** under `sourcePaths`; it is used for warnings/errors (`DirtyWorktreeError` prints each one, `source.go:96-108`) but is not emitted in JSON.

Digest resolution convention: `sha-<commit>` tags (`internal/source/digest.go:15-18`), resolved through the registry so multi-arch indexes pin correctly (`ResolveDigests`, `digest.go:56-72`).

---

## 5. Full JSON output field inventory (`internal/deploy/result.go`)

`deploy` / `deploy promote` → `Result` (`result.go:7-48`): `component, domain, system, environment, sourceCommit, appName, overlayPath, pins[], changed, applied, revision?, release?, promotedFrom?, upstreams[]?, syncPolicy, syncStatus?, healthStatus?, syncedRevision?`

`ResultPin` (`result.go:228-236`): `image, previous?, digest, tag?`

`deploy sync` → `SyncResult` (`result.go:53-77`): `component, domain, system, environment, appName, overlayPath, revision, requested, syncPolicy, syncStatus?, healthStatus?, syncedRevision?`

`deploy diff` → `DiffResult` (`result.go:81-126`): `component, domain, system, environment, appName, overlayPath, pending, synced?, applied, changed, diff?, removedResources[]?, subject?, release?, promotedFrom?, sourceCommit?, deployedBy?, syncPolicy, syncStatus?, healthStatus?`. **`diff` carries the full rendered Kubernetes diff inside the JSON** — that is the highest-volume, most sensitive payload of any command here, because ArgoCD renders the whole Application (Secrets included) at two revisions (`diff.go:128-138`, `kustomize.NormalizeJSON`).

`deploy status` → `StatusResult` (`result.go:161-183`): `component, domain, system, kind, environments[], consistent`; each `EnvironmentStatus` (`result.go:186-225`): `environment, appName, overlayPath, onboarded, reason?, release?, sourceCommit?, pins[]?, revision?, deployedAt?, syncPolicy, syncStatus?, healthStatus?, syncedRevision?, pending`. Plain output is the table `COMPONENT ENV RELEASE DIGEST AGE SYNC HEALTH` (`status.go:261`).

`deploy init` → `InitResult` (above).

---

## 6. Environment / context / config concepts

### Per-user config (`~/.config/intropy/config.yaml`)

```go
// internal/config/config.go:46-55
type Config struct {
	GitopsRepo   string `yaml:"gitopsRepo"`
	ArgocdServer string `yaml:"argocdServer"`
}
```
Precedence flag > env > file (`config.go:129-134`); env vars `INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO`, plus borrowed `ARGOCD_SERVER` / `ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN` (`config.go:31-38`). Unknown keys rejected.

### `deploy.yaml` at the GitOps repo root — the repository-level contract

```go
// internal/gitops/config.go:59-75
type DeployConfig struct {
	SchemaVersion int    `yaml:"schemaVersion"`
	Registry      string `yaml:"registry"`
	MinimumCliVersion string `yaml:"minimumCliVersion"`
	Platform PlatformConfig `yaml:"platform"`
	Argocd       ArgocdConfig                 `yaml:"argocd"`
	Environments map[string]EnvironmentConfig `yaml:"environments"`
}
// :82-93
type PlatformConfig struct { Provider, Pubsub, SecretStore string }   // "azure"/"beebyte", "rabbitmq"/"servicebus", "kubernetes"/"azure.keyvault"/"vault"
// :96-105
type ArgocdConfig struct { Server string; AppNamespace string }        // appNamespace e.g. customer-wsf
// :108-126
type EnvironmentConfig struct {
	Sync string `yaml:"sync"`                                  // "auto" | "manual"
	PromotesFrom []string `yaml:"promotesFrom"`
	RequireSourceHealthy bool `yaml:"requireSourceHealthy"`
	Scratch bool `yaml:"scratch"`                              // parsed, never acted on
}
```

`PromotionOrder()` (`config.go:223-279`) is a topological sort of `promotesFrom` — that graph *is* the promotion pipeline, and both `status` row order and `init`'s default overlay set come from it.

### `component.yaml` per component

```go
// internal/gitops/config.go:129-154
type ComponentConfig struct {
	SchemaVersion int    `yaml:"schemaVersion"`
	Name          string `yaml:"name"`
	Kind          string `yaml:"kind"`          // "service" (default) | "shared"
	SourcePaths []string `yaml:"sourcePaths"`   // paths in the SOURCE repo
	Images []ImageRef    `yaml:"images"`
	Environments []string `yaml:"environments"`
}
type ImageRef struct { Name string `yaml:"name"` }
```

### Coordinates / ArgoCD app naming

```go
// internal/gitops/layout.go:14-18
type Coordinate struct { Domain, System, Component string }
// :23-25  RelPath  = domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>
// :29-31  OverlayRelPath(env) = <RelPath>/overlays/<env>   (== ArgoCD spec.source.path)
// :39-41
func (c Coordinate) AppName(env string) string {
	return strings.Join([]string{c.Domain, c.System, c.Component, env}, "-")
}
```

"Customer" is not a modelled concept in code — it appears only as (a) the GitOps repo URL path, and (b) `argocd.appNamespace` (`config.go:99-104`, e.g. `customer-wsf`). One repo = one customer, by convention.

---

## 7. Local on-disk footprint and credential surface

- **GitOps cache**: `<os.UserCacheDir()>/intropy/gitops/<first-16-hex-of-sha256(url)>` plus a sibling `.lock` file (`internal/gitops/repository.go:151-157`, `:189-192`, `:198-211`). It is a full clone of the customer's GitOps repo, retained after the run (`Close` keeps the checkout, `:138-149`), hard-reset + `git clean` on each open. `deploy init` may leave a local `deploy-init/*` branch behind (it switches back in a `defer`, `init.go:870-874`).
- **Reads** `~/.config/argocd/config` for the ArgoCD **bearer token** (`internal/argocd/config.go:27-58`; `CLIUser.AuthToken`, plus `insecure`/`plain-text` flags), or `ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- **Reads Docker credential store** for registry auth (`internal/registry/client.go:61-68`).
- **Writes nothing** under `.intropy/` — that file (`.intropy/scaffold.json`, `internal/template/scaffold.go:18`, struct at `:58-82`: `schemaVersion, template, owner, repo, version, values, role, blockKind, dataFlow, dependsOn[]`) is written by `int create` and only **read** by `deploy init` (via `template.ListScaffolds`, `internal/template/scaffold_list.go:52`) to derive app-ids, dirs, and the `.scaffold` template values.
- Nothing here invokes `kubectl`; `deploy diff`/`sync`/`status`/`promote` talk to the ArgoCD REST API (`internal/argocd/client.go:141-243`: `Get`, `Refresh`, `Sync`, `Manifests`, `Events`), and `Application` exposes `metadata.name/namespace`, `spec.source.path`, `status.sync.{status,revision}`, `status.health.{status,message}`, `status.operationState.{phase,message}` (`client.go:101-131`).

---

## 8. Notable asymmetries worth flagging

1. **`Manifest.Source.Repo` holds the GitOps URL, not the source repo URL** (`release/create.go:137`) — a customer-identifying URL is baked into an immutable artifact stored in that customer's registry.
2. **`org.opencontainers.image.description` leaks a commit subject** into unauthenticated-readable registry metadata for any public/loosely-scoped registry (`release/artifact.go:86`).
3. **`deploy diff -o json` embeds fully rendered manifests as a unified diff**, including anything in `base/secrets/` — the only command that ships cluster-resource content rather than references.
4. **`Deploy-By` / `CreatedBy`** put an operator email into git history and OCI manifests, sourced from `GITLAB_USER_EMAIL`/`GITHUB_ACTOR`/`USER`.
5. `InitResult.Placeholders` is an explicit map of "where the unset secrets are", which is useful to an operator and equally useful to anyone reading the pushed `deploy-init/*` branch.
6. `deploy status`'s `consistent` bool is the only cross-environment aggregate; exit code is always 0, so gating requires JSON (`deploy_status.go:37-38`, `status.go:222-238`).</result>

# Surfacing `deploy` + `release` data in the dashboard

*(draft — plan agent still reporting)*

## Context

`intropy dashboard` is a **workspace-local, offline, read-only** view. Its package doc
is explicit (`internal/dashboard/server.go:1`): the only thing it executes is each
system host's `graph` verb. Everything else comes off the local disk:

| Source | Reader |
| --- | --- |
| `.intropy/scaffold.json` | `template.ListScaffolds(root)` → `handlers.go:130 scan()` |
| host `graph` verb (`topology.intropy.io/v1`) | `topology.RunGraph` → `topology.go:25 hostGraphProvider` |
| `local/dapr-components/*.yaml` | `components.go:48 readComponents` |
| `src/Process/Steps/*` | `handlers.go:355 listNames` |
| `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` | `handlers.go:342 readDoc` |
| `messages/<connector>.md` | `messagedocs.go:65 readMessageDocs` |

So the catalog answers **"what did we build?"** — Template, Version, Source, Path,
Values, Pipeline steps, Dapr components, README (`DetailPanel.tsx:28-84`).

It cannot answer **"what is actually running, where, at which version, and is it
healthy?"** — even though that answer already exists as fully-structured JSON in
`intropy deploy status` and `intropy release view`. Today you have to leave the
dashboard and run a CLI command per component to get it.

This plan closes that gap.

## Data already structured and available

### `deploy status` — per component, per environment
`internal/deploy/result.go:161`

- `StatusResult{Component, Domain, System, Kind, Environments[], Consistent}`
- `EnvironmentStatus{Environment, AppName, OverlayPath, Onboarded, Reason,
  Release, SourceCommit, Pins[], Revision, DeployedAt, SyncPolicy, SyncStatus,
  HealthStatus, SyncedRevision, Pending}`
- `ResultPin{Image, Previous, Digest, Tag}`
- `Consistent` is the headline claim: *promotion copies digests rather than
  rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes "prod runs the bits staging tested"
  a fact rather than a hope.*

### `release` — per component, per version
`internal/release/manifest.go:29`

- `Manifest{SchemaVersion, Component, Version, CreatedAt, CreatedBy,
  Source{Commit,Ref,Repo}, Images[]{Name,Digest}, Notes, Changes[]{Commit,Subject},
  ChangeBasis{Kind,Version,Commit,Ref}}`
- `ChangeBasis.Describe()` already renders the human sentence.
- `release.ListVersions(ctx, reg, releasesRepo)` (`artifact.go:126`) already
  enumerates every published version — a release *history* is a one-liner away.

### GitOps repo facts — free once the clone is open
`internal/gitops/config.go`

- `DeployConfig{Registry, MinimumCliVersion, Platform{Provider,Pubsub,SecretStore},

Note the tiers are *nested*, and the cheap tier is the valuable one:

| Tier | Needs | Gives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **0** local disk only | nothing new | today's catalog |
| **1** GitOps clone | `git`, repo URL, network once | envs, versions, digests, promotion graph, deploy **history**, placeholders, platform facts, `Consistent` |
| **2** + ArgoCD | token | `SyncStatus`, `HealthStatus`, `Pending` |
| **3** + OCI registry | registry auth | release notes, changes, `changeBasis` |

Tier 1 carries most of the value and has one dependency. Tiers 2 and 3 must degrade
to *"not asked"*, never to *"unhealthy"* or *"no releases"*.

## Suggestions, ranked

### 1. Deployment ladder in the catalog detail panel — *highest value / effort*
A new `Section` in `DetailPanel.tsx` showing the environments in **promotion order**
(`DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()`), one card or row per env: env name, release
version, short digest, age, sync policy, sync/health chips. Under it, the verdict
sentence `deploy status` already computes from `Consistent`:

> all 3 environments run `sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc` — same bits, promoted rather than rebuilt

This is `intropy deploy status` rendered where you were already looking. It turns
the catalog from a build-time inventory into an operational one.

Honesty requirements, all already modelled in the Go types: `Onboarded: false` +
`Reason` renders as "not onboarded here — <reason>", *not* as an empty cell;
`Kind: shared` renders "shared — nothing to pin"; a tag-pinned overlay says so.

### 2. Deployment history timeline — *biggest latent win*
Build the `deploy history` reader the trailers were designed for (`publish.go:18`
promises it), then serve it to both the CLI and the dashboard. Per component, per
env: a reverse-chronological list of `who / when / version / source commit /
deploy-or-promotion`. Offline after the clone; no new dependency beyond tier 1.

This is the audit trail the trailers exist to provide and that nothing currently
reads back.

### 3. Sidebar status indicator
The sidebar tree (`Sidebar.tsx:190`) shows only name + path, so the catalog is not
scannable. A small dot per integration makes it so:

- green — onboarded everywhere it declares, consistent, healthy
- amber — drift, or a committed change ArgoCD has not applied (`Pending`) — note
  that for a `sync: manual` env this is *a gate waiting*, not a fault, and must
  read that way
- grey — not onboarded
- hollow / absent — GitOps not configured (i.e. *unknown*, not *bad*)

### 4. A third view: fleet deployment matrix
`type View = 'catalog' | 'flow'` becomes `| 'deployments'`. One table, every
component × every environment, cells showing version + health. **This is new
capability, not a re-rendering**: `deploy status` is one component at a time, and
`gitops.ListComponents(root)` (`layout.go:142`) already enumerates the whole tree
in a single pass, so the fleet view costs the same clone as one component.

Also the natural home for repo-level facts: registry, `Platform{Provider, Pubsub,
SecretStore}`, the ArgoCD server, and the `promotesFrom` graph drawn as lanes.

### 5. Release history section
Newest-first list from `release.ListVersions` (`artifact.go:126`), each expandable
to `Notes`, `Changes[]{Commit,Subject}`, `Images[]{Name,Digest}`,
`ChangeBasis.Describe()`, `CreatedAt`/`CreatedBy`. Tier 3, so it must degrade
cleanly. Cross-link: the version a given env runs is a link into this list — which
answers *"what actually changed between staging and prod?"* in one click.

Caveat found while reading: releases are addressed off
`ReleasesRepo(comp.Images[0].Name)` (`view.go:62`) — the **first** declared image.
A multi-image component has one release stream; the UI should not imply otherwise.

### 6. Onboarding gaps panel
Outstanding `REPLACE-ME-*` placeholders per component, scanned from the component's
directory in the GitOps clone. Answers "is this deployable yet?" and turns the
remaining onboarding work into a bounded list. `deploy/placeholder.go` has the
scanner (`scanPlaceholders`, currently unexported).

### 7. Enrich the flow view's integration nodes
`FlowDetail.tsx` already has a working drawer, but its `FlowSelection` union only
covers `topic` and `connector` — clicking an *integration* node just changes the
selection with no drawer. Widening it with `{kind:'integration'; path}` and
reusing the deployment ladder would put "what version is this running" on the
canvas.

### Not recommended
- **Making the dashboard always fetch GitOps on startup.** It would turn a
  zero-dependency local tool into one that fails or hangs without network and a
  configured repo. Lazy-on-first-request with an explicit refresh (exactly the
  `topologyProvider` + `topoMu/topoLoaded` pattern at `handlers.go:258`) is the
  established answer in this codebase.
- **Writes from the dashboard** (trigger a deploy / promote / sync). The package
  doc's read-only promise is load-bearing, and `deploy promote`'s refusals and the
  production gate are deliberately CLI-and-review-shaped.
- **Inferring anything.** No guessing that a component is deployed because a
  directory exists. The codebase is consistent about this (`FlowView.tsx:219`
  renders an empty state rather than a guessed graph) and the deploy types encode
  it (`Onboarded`, `Reason`, `ChangeBasis`).

### Known sharp edge
Per memory, `config.yaml` holds a single flat `gitopsRepo` and **component names
collide across customers**; contexts are a pending redesign. The workspace→GitOps
join is by `{domain, system, component}` and can genuinely be ambiguous
(`gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` already exists at `layout.go:53`). An ambiguous
match must render as ambiguous, not resolved arbitrarily.

| `src/Process/Steps/*` | `handlers.go:355 listNames` |
| `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` | `handlers.go:342 readDoc` |
| `messages/<connector>.md` | `messagedocs.go:65 readMessageDocs` |

Values, Pipeline steps, Dapr components, README (`DetailPanel.tsx:28-84`).

healthy?"** — even though that answer already exists as fully-structured JSON in

  Release, SourceCommit, Pins[], Revision, DeployedAt, SyncPolicy, SyncStatus,
  HealthStatus, SyncedRevision, Pending}`

- `Consistent` is the headline claim: *promotion copies digests rather than
  rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes "prod runs the bits staging tested"

## 2. The release record (`release create` / `release view`)

### Storage location

**Not** a local file and **not** the gitops repo. It is a tag-addressed **OCI artifact** in the same registry as the images, in a sibling repository:

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:30
const ReleasesRepoSuffix = "/releases"
// :43
func ReleasesRepo(image string) string {
	return strings.TrimSuffix(image, "/") + ReleasesRepoSuffix
}
// :48
func Ref(releasesRepo, version string) string { return releasesRepo + ":" + version }
```

The repo is derived from `component.yaml`'s `images[0].name` (`internal/release/create.go:102`), so e.g. `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/order-extractor/releases:1.4.2`. Media types (immutable by design):

```go

MediaTypeJSON = "application/vnd.integrio.release.v1+json"
```

### The manifest itself

```go

	SchemaVersion int         `json:"schemaVersion"`
	Component     string      `json:"component"`
	Version       string      `json:"version"`
	CreatedAt     time.Time   `json:"createdAt"`
	CreatedBy     string      `json:"createdBy"`
	Source        Source      `json:"source"`

	Notes         string      `json:"notes"`

// :43-47

// :60-63

// :84-93

`CreatedBy` is scraped from the environment:

### OCI annotations (visible in a registry UI without pulling the layer)

```go

Annotations: map[string]string{
	AnnotationComponent:                    m.Component,        // io.intropy.release.component
	AnnotationCommit:                       m.Source.Commit,    // io.intropy.release.source-commit
	"org.opencontainers.image.title":       m.Component,
	"org.opencontainers.image.version":     m.Version,
	"org.opencontainers.image.created":     m.CreatedAt.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z"),

### Ancestry / changelog derivation

`PreviousRelease` (`internal/release/changelog.go:44`) lists *all* tags in the releases repo (`ListVersions` → `reg.ListTags`), pulls each manifest, and picks the nearest ancestor by `git merge-base --is-ancestor` rather than version sort. ## 7. Local on-disk footprint and credential surface

- **GitOps cache**: `<os.UserCacheDir()>/intropy/gitops/<first-16-hex-of-sha256(url)>` plus a sibling `.lock` file (`internal/gitops/repository.go:151-157`, `:189-192`, `:198-211`). - **Reads Docker credential store** for registry auth (`internal/registry/client.go:61-68`).
- **Writes nothing** under `.intropy/` — that file (`.intropy/scaffold.json`, `internal/template/scaffold.go:18`, struct at `:58-82`: `schemaVersion, template, owner, repo, version, values, role, blockKind, dataFlow, dependsOn[]`) is written by `int create` and only **read** by `deploy init` (via `template.ListScaffolds`, `internal/template/scaffold_list.go:52`) to derive app-ids, dirs, and the `.scaffold` template values.

## 8. Notable asymmetries worth flagging

1. **`Manifest.Source.Repo` holds the GitOps URL, not the source repo URL** (`release/create.go:137`) — a customer-identifying URL is baked into an immutable artifact stored in that customer's registry.
2. **`org.opencontainers.image.description` leaks a commit subject** into unauthenticated-readable registry metadata for any public/loosely-scoped registry (`release/artifact.go:86`).
3. **`deploy diff -o json` embeds fully rendered manifests as a unified diff**, including anything in `base/secrets/` — the only command that ships cluster-resource content rather than references.
4. **`Deploy-By` / `CreatedBy`** put an operator email into git history and OCI manifests, sourced from `GITLAB_USER_EMAIL`/`GITHUB_ACTOR`/`USER`.
5. `InitResult.Placeholders` is an explicit map of "where the unset secrets are", which is useful to an operator and equally useful to anyone reading the pushed `deploy-init/*` branch.
6. `deploy status`'s `consistent` bool is the only cross-environment aggregate; exit code is always 0, so gating requires JSON (`deploy_status.go:37-38`, `status.go:222-238`).</result>

## 2. The release record (`release create` / `release view`)

### Storage location

**Not** a local file and **not** the gitops repo. It is a tag-addressed **OCI artifact** in the same registry as the images, in a sibling repository:

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:30
const ReleasesRepoSuffix = "/releases"
// :43
func ReleasesRepo(image string) string {
	return strings.TrimSuffix(image, "/") + ReleasesRepoSuffix
}
// :48
func Ref(releasesRepo, version string) string { return releasesRepo + ":" + version }
```

The repo is derived from `component.yaml`'s `images[0].name` (`internal/release/create.go:102`), so e.g. `harbor.intropy.io/integrations/order-extractor/releases:1.4.2`. Media types (immutable by design):

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:16-18
ArtifactType  = "application/vnd.integrio.release.v1"
MediaTypeJSON = "application/vnd.integrio.release.v1+json"
```

### The manifest itself

```go
// internal/release/manifest.go:22
const SchemaVersion = 1

// internal/release/manifest.go:29-40
type Manifest struct {
	SchemaVersion int         `json:"schemaVersion"`
	Component     string      `json:"component"`
	Version       string      `json:"version"`
	CreatedAt     time.Time   `json:"createdAt"`
	CreatedBy     string      `json:"createdBy"`
	Source        Source      `json:"source"`
	Images        []Image     `json:"images"`
	Notes         string      `json:"notes"`
	Changes       []Change    `json:"changes"`
	ChangeBasis   ChangeBasis `json:"changeBasis"`
}

// :43-47
type Source struct {
	Commit string `json:"commit"`
	Ref    string `json:"ref"`
	Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"`
}

// :54-57
type Image struct {
	Name   string `json:"name"`
	Digest string `json:"digest"`
}

// :60-63
type Change struct {
	Commit  string `json:"commit"`
	Subject string `json:"subject"`
}

// :84-93
type ChangeBasis struct {
	Kind string `json:"kind"`
	// Version and Commit identify the predecessor when Kind is BasisRelease.
	Version string `json:"version,omitempty"`
	Commit  string `json:"commit,omitempty"`
	// Ref is what the operator passed to --since when Kind is BasisExplicit.
	Ref string `json:"ref,omitempty"`
}
```

`ChangeBasis.Kind` ∈ `{"initial","release","explicit"}` (`manifest.go:70-76`). Note **`Source.Repo` is the GitOps repository URL, not the source repo** — `create.go:137` sets `Source{Commit: commit, Ref: opts.Ref, Repo: repoURL}` where `repoURL` came from `RequireGitopsRepo()`. That URL frequently encodes the customer (`git@gitlab.com:integrio/intropy/customers/acme/gitops.git`, README:784) and is therefore embedded in every published release manifest.

`CreatedBy` is scraped from the environment:

```go
// internal/release/create.go:292-299
func committer() string {
	for _, key := range []string{"GITLAB_USER_EMAIL", "GITHUB_ACTOR", "USER"} {
		if v := os.Getenv(key); v != "" { return v }
	}
	return ""
}
```

(An identical `committer()` exists at `internal/deploy/publish.go:232`.) So an operator email/username lands in both the release manifest and every deploy commit.

### OCI annotations (visible in a registry UI without pulling the layer)

```go
// internal/release/artifact.go:79-87
Annotations: map[string]string{
	AnnotationComponent:                    m.Component,        // io.intropy.release.component
	AnnotationCommit:                       m.Source.Commit,    // io.intropy.release.source-commit
	"org.opencontainers.image.title":       m.Component,
	"org.opencontainers.image.version":     m.Version,
	"org.opencontainers.image.created":     m.CreatedAt.UTC().Format("2006-01-02T15:04:05Z"),
	"org.opencontainers.image.revision":    m.Source.Commit,
	"org.opencontainers.image.description": firstLine(m.Notes),
},
```

`firstLine(m.Notes)` is the **first commit subject** of the changelog, promoted into a registry annotation.

### Ancestry / changelog derivation

`PreviousRelease` (`internal/release/changelog.go:44`) lists *all* tags in the releases repo (`ListVersions` → `reg.ListTags`), pulls each manifest, and picks the nearest ancestor by `git merge-base --is-ancestor` rather than version sort. Consequences for information flow: creating one release **reads every other release manifest of that component**, and `Changes` is `git log <prev>..<commit> -- <sourcePaths>` (`changelog.go:108-119`) — i.e. **commit SHAs + subjects scoped to the component's `sourcePaths`** are copied verbatim into the manifest and into `Notes` as `- <subject>` lines (`RenderNotes`, `changelog.go:122`).

### Git tag side-effect

```go
// internal/release/create.go:244-246
func TagName(component, version string) string { return component + "/v" + version }
// :280-282  annotated tag message
func tagMessage(m *Manifest) string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s\n\n%s", m.Component, m.Version, m.Notes)
}
```

Pushed to `origin` in the **source** repo. Failure is a warning only (`create.go:271-275`).

### `release create` machine-readable result

```go

type Result struct {
	Component string `json:"component"`
	Version   string `json:"version"`
	Ref       string `json:"ref"`      // full OCI ref
	Digest    string `json:"digest"`   // manifest digest
	Created   bool   `json:"created"`
	Tag       string `json:"tag"`
	Tagged    bool   `json:"tagged"`

}
```

`release view -o json` emits the raw `Manifest` (`internal/release/view.go:73-77`).

- Writes into the cached GitOps checkout and pushes a **branch, never the default branch**:
  ```go

  // :192
  branch := initBranchPrefix + facts.Domain + "-" + facts.System

- Tree shape: `domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/…` plus a shared host dir:
  ```go

  ```
- Two templates, fetched from the **external** library `integrio-intropy/intropy-templates` (`internal/template/github.go:14-15`):
  ```go

  TemplateDeployHost      = "deploy-host"
  TemplateDeployComponent = "deploy-component"

The actual manifest bodies live in that other repo. ```go

WorkloadDeployment = "deployment"

Three reserved injections plus seeds. Seeds (`init.go:743-772`):

	"provider": facts.Platform.Provider, "pubsub": facts.Platform.Pubsub,

Reserved `.scaffold` = the component's **entire `.intropy/scaffold.json` `values` map** (`init.go:816-821`) — i.e. whatever `int create` recorded is available to any manifest template.

Reserved `.topology` = the derived model, fully sorted for byte-identical re-renders:

```go

## 7. Local on-disk footprint and credential surface

- **GitOps cache**: `<os.UserCacheDir()>/intropy/gitops/<first-16-hex-of-sha256(url)>` plus a sibling `.lock` file (`internal/gitops/repository.go:151-157`, `:189-192`, `:198-211`). - **Reads** `~/.config/argocd/config` for the ArgoCD **bearer token** (`internal/argocd/config.go:27-58`; `CLIUser.AuthToken`, plus `insecure`/`plain-text` flags), or `ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN`.
- **Reads Docker credential store** for registry auth (`internal/registry/client.go:61-68`).
- **Writes nothing** under `.intropy/` — that file (`.intropy/scaffold.json`, `internal/template/scaffold.go:18`, struct at `:58-82`: `schemaVersion, template, owner, repo, version, values, role, blockKind, dataFlow, dependsOn[]`) is written by `int create` and only **read** by `deploy init` (via `template.ListScaffolds`, `internal/template/scaffold_list.go:52`) to derive app-ids, dirs, and the `.scaffold` template values.

## 8. Notable asymmetries worth flagging

1. **`Manifest.Source.Repo` holds the GitOps URL, not the source repo URL** (`release/create.go:137`) — a customer-identifying URL is baked into an immutable artifact stored in that customer's registry.
2. **`org.opencontainers.image.description` leaks a commit subject** into unauthenticated-readable registry metadata for any public/loosely-scoped registry (`release/artifact.go:86`).
3. **`deploy diff -o json` embeds fully rendered manifests as a unified diff**, including anything in `base/secrets/` — the only command that ships cluster-resource content rather than references.
4. **`Deploy-By` / `CreatedBy`** put an operator email into git history and OCI manifests, sourced from `GITLAB_USER_EMAIL`/`GITHUB_ACTOR`/`USER`.
5. `InitResult.Placeholders` is an explicit map of "where the unset secrets are", which is useful to an operator and equally useful to anyone reading the pushed `deploy-init/*` branch.
6. `deploy status`'s `consistent` bool is the only cross-environment aggregate; exit code is always 0, so gating requires JSON (`deploy_status.go:37-38`, `status.go:222-238`).</result>

### The resolution: read the cache, refresh on demand

The dashboard does **not** need `openSession`. `gitops.CachedRoot(override)`
(`repository.go:165`) resolves the already-cached checkout with **no network, no
lock, and no hard reset**, failing cleanly with `no cached checkout of <url> yet`.
The shell completions already rely on exactly this (`cmd/intropy/deploy.go:122`:
*"Every completion here reads the local cache only"*), so the precedent is
established.

That makes the shape obvious, and identical to `topologyProvider`:

- **startup** — unchanged; no network, no new required config
- **first `/api/deploy` request** — `CachedRoot()` + `gitops.ListComponents` +
  `readOverlayState` per env, all off local disk. Cached in `apiServer` behind a
  mutex like `topoMu`.
- **`POST /api/deploy/refresh`** — the only place that pays for `gitops.Open`
  (lock + fetch), then optionally ArgoCD and the registry.
- **no cache at all** — a first-class "not fetched yet" state with the refresh
  affordance, clearly distinct from "not deployed".

The offline invariant survives for the default path.

Per memory, `config.yaml` holds a single flat `gitopsRepo` and **component names
collide across customers**; contexts are a pending redesign. The workspace→GitOps

### Known sharp edges
- **Ambiguous joins.** `config.yaml` holds a single flat `gitopsRepo` and component
  names collide across customers; contexts are a pending redesign. The
  workspace→GitOps join is by `{domain, system, component}` and can genuinely be
  ambiguous — `gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` already exists (`layout.go:53`). An
  ambiguous match must render as ambiguous, never resolved arbitrarily.
- **`Manifest.Source.Repo` is the *GitOps* repo URL, not the source repo**
  (`release/create.go:137` passes `repoURL` from `RequireGitopsRepo()`). Do not
  label it "source repository" in the UI.
- **Multi-image components have one release stream**, addressed off
  `ReleasesRepo(comp.Images[0].Name)` (`view.go:62`). The UI must not imply
  per-image releases.
- **`EnvironmentConfig.Scratch` is parsed but never acted on** (`config.go:125`).
  Don't build UI meaning onto it.
- **`Deploy-By` / `CreatedBy` carry operator emails**, scraped from
  `GITLAB_USER_EMAIL` / `GITHUB_ACTOR` / `USER` (`publish.go:232`,
  `create.go:292`). Fine for a localhost tool bound to `127.0.0.1` by default —
  worth remembering if the dashboard is ever bound wider.

# Surfacing deploy + release state in the Integration Catalog

## 0. The one finding that shapes everything

`internal/gitops/repository.go:159` already has the primitive this feature needs:

```go
// CachedRoot returns the existing cached checkout for the configured GitOps
// repository.
//
// It never clones or fetches. This backs shell completion, which has to be
// instant and must not touch the network...
func CachedRoot(gitopsRepoOverride string) (string, error)
```

It resolves config → URL → `CheckoutDir` → stat, and **takes no lock**. Four commands already depend on it (`cmd/intropy/deploy.go:128,146`, `release.go:24`, `deploy_init.go:130`) for exactly the reason the dashboard needs it: an instant, offline, never-fails read of deployment facts.

So the answer to hard problem #1 is not a flag. It is: **the dashboard reads the checkout the CLI already left on disk, and says out loud which checkout that was and when.** Phase 1 adds no network, no lock, no token, no flag — and the offline invariant in `internal/dashboard/server.go:1` survives verbatim for every `GET`.

The decisive argument against always-fetching is not latency, it is `internal/gitops/repository.go` `acquireLock`: `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`, and on contention it returns

> `another intropy deploy is already using the cached GitOps checkout (…); wait for it to finish`

A dashboard that fetched on page load would either break a concurrent `intropy deploy` or fail with that message in a background browser tab. Neither is acceptable for a long-lived viewer. A `--deploy`/`--gitops-repo` boot flag is also wrong as the *enable* switch: the dashboard outlives the decision, and a tri-state honest report is strictly better than a mode.

---

## Phase 1 — the smallest honest useful slice

**Scope:** every environment's release, digest, age and sync-policy for every catalogued integration, read offline from the cached checkout, with a four-way distinction between *not configured*, *no checkout*, *not onboarded*, and *not deployed*. No ArgoCD. No registry. No new CLI flags.

Note what comes free: `EnvironmentStatus.Release` is read from the overlay's `deploy.internal/release` annotation (`status.go:128`), so **the release version each environment runs is Phase 1 with zero registry access.** Only the release *manifest* (notes, changes, `ChangeBasis`) needs the registry, and that is Phase 4.

### 1a. Break `readOverlayState`'s dependency on `*gitops.Repository`

This is the whole unlock. `internal/deploy/status.go:106` takes `repo *gitops.Repository` but only ever uses `repo.Root` (via `gitops.ResolveOverlay`) and `repo.Git` (via `LastCommitAt`). Nothing it does needs a lock.

```go
// internal/deploy/status.go — changed signature
func readOverlayState(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client, coord gitops.Coordinate,
	comp *gitops.ComponentConfig, env string) EnvironmentStatus
```

`g == nil` skips the `Revision`/`DeployedAt` history read (both are already documented as "empty when the path has no history", so nil is an existing, honest shape rather than a new one). In-package callers become `readOverlayState(ctx, repo.Root, &repo.Git, …)`. `observeArgo` (`status.go:157`) needs the same treatment for its `revisionContains(repo)` call — leave it taking `*gitops.Repository`, it is ArgoCD-only and Phase 3.

### 1b. Extract the per-component read from `Status`

```go
// internal/deploy/status.go
// ComponentStatus reads one component's state in every environment it declares,
// from a GitOps checkout that is already on disk. It is Status without the
// session, the ArgoCD call and the report: no lock, no network, no output.
// Nothing here fails — an unreadable environment comes back Onboarded false
// with a Reason, which is the same contract readOverlayState has.
func ComponentStatus(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client,
	deployCfg *gitops.DeployConfig, coord gitops.Coordinate,
	comp *gitops.ComponentConfig) StatusResult
```

Body is `status.go:52-60` plus the `StatusResult` assembly from `reportStatus` (`status.go:244-251`). `Status` then becomes session → `locateComponent` → `ComponentStatus` → `observeArgo(res.Environments)` → `reportStatus`. `statusEnvironments`, `readOverlayState`, `consistent`, `pinSignature` are all reused, none duplicated.

**The refactor is done when every existing test in `internal/deploy` passes with zero edits.** That is the "CLI behaves identically" assertion; do not weaken it.

### 1c. Serve the prose, do not re-derive it

`summarise` (`status.go:352`) and `notes` (`status.go:435`) are the honest-reporting layer of this whole feature — the sentences that distinguish "these two run different bits" from "there is nothing to compare here", and that say *"DIGEST is empty by design"* for a shared component. **Reimplementing them in TypeScript is the single most likely way this feature becomes dishonest**, because the Go tests assert on that prose and React would silently drift from it.

Add two additive fields, which `StatusResult`'s own doc licenses ("field names are stable and additive-only"):

```go
// StatusResult, in internal/deploy/result.go:668
	// Summary and Notes are the sentences the plain table prints beneath
	// itself: what the environments collectively run, and the qualifications
	// — what could not be read, what pins a tag, what is waiting. They travel
	// in the result so that a second presenter cannot draw a different
	// conclusion from the same rows than the table does.
	Summary string   `json:"summary"`
	Notes   []string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
```

`ComponentStatus` fills them via the existing functions; `reportStatus` keeps calling them for the terminal, or reads them back off the result (prefer the latter — one call site). Side effect: `deploy status -o json` gains prose it was previously missing, which is an improvement. If the team wants the CLI's JSON frozen instead, the fallback is a dashboard-local wrapper struct — but I recommend against it, because then two structs carry the same claim.

### 1d. `Survey` — every component, one pass, no lock

```go
// internal/deploy/survey.go  (new file)

// SurveyOptions configures Survey.
type SurveyOptions struct {
	// Root is a GitOps checkout that is already on disk. Survey never
	// clones, fetches or locks it: the caller either owns a session or, like
	// the dashboard, is reading the checkout an earlier command left behind.
	Root string

	// Git reads each overlay's last-changed commit, which is what dates a
	// deployment. Nil skips it — one `git log` per environment per component
	// is the only cost in here worth being able to decline.
	Git *git.Client

	// Coords narrows the survey. Empty means every component in the tree.
	Coords []gitops.Coordinate
}

// SurveyEntry is one component's state, or the reason it has none.
type SurveyEntry struct {
	Coordinate gitops.Coordinate
	Status     *StatusResult

	// Error is why this component could not be described — an unreadable or
	// invalid component.yaml. Status is then nil. One malformed component
	// never costs the caller the rest of the tree.
	Error string
}

// Survey reads every component's state from one checkout.
//
// This is deploy status for a whole repository, minus the session: N calls to
// Status would take the exclusive checkout lock N times and fetch N times, and
// would only be able to hand back rendered text. Nothing here fails.
func Survey(ctx context.Context, opts SurveyOptions) (cfg *gitops.DeployConfig, entries []SurveyEntry, errs []string)
```

Implementation is `gitops.ListComponents(root)` (one glob, `layout.go:142`) → `LoadComponentConfig` → `ComponentStatus`. Entries sorted by `Coordinate.String()`, as `ListComponents` already returns them.

**Cost:** with `Git` non-nil this is `N×M` `git log -1 -- <path>` subprocesses on a warm local repo — roughly 1 s for 30 components × 3 envs. That is fine because it sits behind the lazy cache, which today already fronts a *dotnet build*. Do not pre-optimise; if measurement demands it later, one `git log --name-only --format` pass over `domains/` replaces the whole loop.

**Torn reads:** a concurrent `intropy deploy` does `ResetHard` + `Clean` in that directory, so a lockless read can see an inconsistent tree. Two honest mitigations, both cheap: (i) every file read here already degrades to `Onboarded:false` + `Reason` rather than failing, so a torn read shows as one bad row that the next refresh fixes; (ii) the report carries the HEAD sha that was read. Do **not** add `LOCK_SH` to `acquireLock` in Phase 1 — it changes `deploy`'s exclusivity story. Note it as an optional Phase 3 hardening: `gitops.OpenReadOnly(url, cacheRoot) (*Repository, error)` taking `LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB` and never fetching.

### 1e. The join — `internal/dashboard/deploy.go` (new file)

The join is **dashboard policy**, and it belongs where `hostGraphProvider` belongs, for the reason `internal/dashboard/topology.go:29` already states: *"The mechanics live in topology.RunGraph… What stays here is the dashboard's policy."* `gitops` and `deploy` stay ignorant of the workspace identifier space.

The codebase already tells us the rule twice:

- `internal/deploy/init.go:493` — *"the source workspace's own layout, which every customer integrations tree mirrors from the deployment tree: `domains/<domain>/<system>/<project>`"*
- `internal/deploy/initmodel.go:134-141` `matchScaffolds` — *"the toolchain uses two conventions: a component's directory basename, and its scaffold record's `values.appId`. Both are matched — directory first."*

So, in strict precedence, first hit wins:

| # | `matchedBy` | rule |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `"coordinate"` | `summary.Domain == c.Domain && summary.System == c.System && summary.Name == c.Component`, exactly one hit |
| 2 | `"system"` | integration has no domain (sits one level under root): `summary.System == c.System && summary.Name == c.Component`, exactly one hit |
| 3 | `"appId"` | `values.appId == c.Component`, exactly one hit, **and** `summary.System == c.System` |

**There is deliberately no bare-name rule.** `gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` exists precisely because a name occurs in several places, and component names collide across customers. Matching on name alone would attribute another system's production digest to this integration — the worst failure available here, and it must be structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

Outcomes, each with its own field so the UI can say the right sentence:

- **exactly one hit at some tier** → `matched:true`, `matchedBy`, `status`
- **no hit at any tier** → `matched:false`, `matchReason: "<name> has no component.yaml under domains/ — it has not been onboarded to the GitOps repository"`. Candidates listing any same-named components at other coordinates, so a mislaid domain reads as a mislaid domain.
- **more than one hit at a tier** → `matched:false`, `matchReason: "…matches N components; the dashboard will not guess which"`, `candidates: ["orders/order-flow/x", …]`, `status: nil`. Never resolve by picking one; mirror `AmbiguousComponentError`'s stance.
- **components nobody claimed** → `orphans[]`. Deployed things no workspace integration accounts for is a finding, not noise.

### 1f. Endpoints — copy the topology seam exactly

`newHandler`'s parameter list is about to grow twice, so collapse it once:

```go
// internal/dashboard/handlers.go
// providers are the request-independent, cached sources the API reads beyond
// the workspace files: a system host's declared topology, and the GitOps
// checkout's deployment state.
type providers struct {
	topology topologyProvider
	deploy   deployProvider
}

func newHandler(root, version string, p providers) (http.Handler, error)
```

```go
// internal/dashboard/deploy.go

// deployProvider surveys the GitOps repository. Like topologyProvider it never
// fails: an unconfigured repository, an absent checkout or an unreadable one
// each come back as a Source state, because "we do not know" and "it is not
// deployed" must never render the same.
type deployProvider func(ctx context.Context) deploySurvey

// deploySurvey is the raw GitOps side of the report — where it came from, and
// what every component in it looks like. The join to workspace integrations is
// the handler's business, so it stays outside the seam and stays testable from
// a literal survey.
type deploySurvey struct {
	Source     deploySource
	Components []deploy.SurveyEntry
	Errors     []string
}

// cachedCheckoutProvider is the default provider: it reads the checkout the
// CLI's deploy commands leave behind. It clones nothing, fetches nothing and
// locks nothing, so a GET can never touch the network or block a deploy.
func cachedCheckoutProvider(gitopsRepoOverride string) deployProvider
```

Routes, added in `newHandler` beside the topology pair:

```
GET  /api/deploy           → deployReport   (lazy, cached, same mutex pattern as topo*)
POST /api/deploy/refresh   → deployReport   (re-reads the cached checkout; still no network)
```

`POST /api/deploy/refresh` being cache-only in Phase 1 is not a stub — it picks up an `intropy deploy` the user just ran in another terminal, which is the actual workflow. Phase 2 upgrades it to fetch.

Cache state on `apiServer` mirrors `topoMu/topoLoaded/topoEntries/topoErrs` field-for-field: `depMu/depLoaded/depSurvey`.

```go
// deployReport is the /api/deploy payload.
type deployReport struct {
	// Source says where this came from and how current it is. Always present,
	// including when nothing could be read — it is what keeps "no GitOps
	// repository is configured" from rendering as "not deployed".
	Source deploySource `json:"source"`

	// Integrations is one entry per catalogued integration, keyed by the same
	// root-relative path /api/integrations uses. Always an array, and always
	// covers every integration — an unmatched one is present and says why.
	Integrations []integrationDeploy `json:"integrations"`

	// Orphans are components in the GitOps tree that no workspace integration
	// claims: deployed workloads nobody in this workspace accounts for.
	Orphans []deploy.StatusResult `json:"orphans,omitempty"`

	Errors []string `json:"errors,omitempty"`
}

// deploySource states are the four honest answers, never a bool.
const (
	sourceUnconfigured = "unconfigured" // no gitopsRepo by flag, env or file
	sourceNoCheckout   = "no-checkout"  // configured, but never cloned here
	sourceUnreadable   = "unreadable"   // cloned, but no usable deploy.yaml
	sourceReady        = "ready"
)

type deploySource struct {
	State  string `json:"state"`
	// Reason is the CLI's own message, verbatim: RequireGitopsRepo's list of
	// every way to supply the URL, or LoadDeployConfig's complaint. Served
	// rather than restated, so the dashboard cannot tell a user something the
	// command line would not.
	Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
	Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"`

	// Revision and RevisionAt are the cached checkout's HEAD: exactly what was
	// read, and when that commit was made. ReadAt is when the survey ran.
	Revision   string     `json:"revision,omitempty"`
	RevisionAt *time.Time `json:"revisionAt,omitempty"`
	ReadAt     time.Time  `json:"readAt"`

	// Fetched reports whether the checkout was refreshed from the remote.
	// False means this is whatever the last deploy command left on disk.
	Fetched bool `json:"fetched"`

	// Environments are deploy.yaml's environments in promotion order, so the
	// UI can lay out a component onboarded to a subset against the full set.
	Environments []string `json:"environments,omitempty"`
}

type integrationDeploy struct {
	Path        string   `json:"path"`
	Matched     bool     `json:"matched"`
	MatchedBy   string   `json:"matchedBy,omitempty"`   // coordinate | system | appId
	MatchReason string   `json:"matchReason,omitempty"` // why not, when Matched is false
	Candidates  []string `json:"candidates,omitempty"`  // coordinates considered and rejected

	Status *deploy.StatusResult `json:"status,omitempty"`
}
```

**Deliberately not** on `GET /api/integrations/{path}`: that endpoint must stay instant and offline-pure, and N detail requests would each need the same survey anyway. One report request, indexed by path on the client — the same shape `FlowView` already uses for `flow()` + `topologies()`.

### 1g. `web/src/api.ts` — mirror 1:1, as the file header promises

```ts

export interface EnvironmentStatus {
  environment: string
  appName: string
  overlayPath: string
  /** False means no readable overlay here; `reason` says why and everything
   *  below is empty. It is never "not deployed" on its own. */

  reason?: string
  release?: string
  sourceCommit?: string

  pins?: ResultPin[]
  revision?: string
  /** RFC3339. Absent when the overlay path has no history. */
  deployedAt?: string
  syncPolicy: 'auto' | 'manual' | string

   *  about what the overlay pins. */
  syncStatus?: string
  healthStatus?: string
  syncedRevision?: string

}

export interface StatusResult {
  component: string; domain: string; system: string
  /** Declared kind. "shared" means no image to pin, so empty digests are by
   *  design rather than evidence of never having been deployed. */
  kind: 'service' | 'shared' | string
  /** In promotion order: the last entry is the furthest downstream. */
  environments: EnvironmentStatus[]
  consistent: boolean
  /** The sentence `deploy status` prints beneath its table. Rendered as
   *  served — never re-derived from `environments`. */
  summary: string
  notes?: string[]
}

export type DeploySourceState = 'unconfigured' | 'no-checkout' | 'unreadable' | 'ready'
export interface DeploySource {
  state: DeploySourceState
  reason?: string
  repo?: string
  revision?: string
  revisionAt?: string
  readAt: string
  /** False: this is the checkout the last deploy command left behind, not a
   *  fresh read of the remote. */
  fetched: boolean
  environments?: string[]
}
export interface IntegrationDeploy {
  path: string
  matched: boolean
  matchedBy?: 'coordinate' | 'system' | 'appId'
  matchReason?: string
  candidates?: string[]
  status?: StatusResult
}
export interface DeployReport {
  source: DeploySource
  integrations: IntegrationDeploy[]
  orphans?: StatusResult[]
  errors?: string[]
}

// on `api`:
  deploy: () => getJSON<DeployReport>('/api/deploy'),
  refreshDeploy: () => requestJSON<DeployReport>('/api/deploy/refresh', { method: 'POST' }),
```

There is **no frontend test runner** in `web/package.json` (only `tsc -b`), so the only guard on this contract is the Go handler tests. Make them assert literal JSON key names via `map[string]any` lookups, which is already the house style in `dashboard_test.go`.

### 1h. UI — `DetailPanel.tsx`, plus a narrow Sidebar chip

`App.tsx`: one more `useState<DeployReport | null>(null)`, fetched in the existing mount effect next to `listIntegrations()`; a `Map<string, IntegrationDeploy>` derived with `useMemo`; passed to `Sidebar` and `DetailPanel`. **No new `View`.**

`DetailPanel.tsx` — a new `<Section title="Deployment" icon={RocketIcon}>` placed *directly under the meta-grid, above Values*: where an integration runs is more operationally interesting than its scaffold values.

1. **Verdict line** — `status.summary`, rendered as served. Plus a small state marker driven by `consistent`.

2. **Environment table**, one row per environment in served order (last row = furthest downstream, matching the CLI):

   | Environment | Release | Image / digest | Age | Sync | Health |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|

   - *Environment* — name, plus a `manual` chip when `syncPolicy === 'manual'` (an unspent manual gate is a resting state, not a fault), plus a `waiting` chip when `pending`.
   - *Release* — `release`, else `@` + `sourceCommit.slice(0,7)`, else `—`. Same rule as `releaseCell`; the `@` prefix is what stops a commit reading as a version, so keep it.
   - *Image / digest* — **all** pins, one line each (`image` → short digest, `title` = full). This is the one place to improve on the CLI: `digestCell` shows only `pins[0]` because a terminal table has no room, and `notes` has to apologise for it. A web panel has the room, so show them and drop that apology when it arrives in `notes`. A `:tag` pin renders as `:tag` in a warning tone.
   - *Age* — from `deployedAt`, truncated to one unit exactly as `humanAge` does (`119m → 1h`, never `2h`); `—` when absent.
   - *Sync / Health* — as served. When **every** row has both empty, collapse the two columns and print one line instead: *"ArgoCD was not read, so sync and health are unknown — this says nothing about what the overlays pin."* An empty column would read as unhealthy.
   - `onboarded: false` — render the row, muted, with `reason` spanning the data cells. Never omit it: `statusEnvironments` deliberately includes an environment the component declares that `deploy.yaml` does not define, and that omission is the fact an operator most needs.

3. **Notes** — `status.notes` as a muted list under the table.

4. **The unknown states.** No spinner, no empty table — the four states each get their own copy, and this four-way distinction *is* the feature:

   | condition | copy |
   |---|---|
   | `source.state === 'unconfigured'` | "No GitOps repository is configured, so nothing here knows whether this is deployed." + `source.reason` verbatim (which is already `RequireGitopsRepo`'s full list of ways to supply it) |
   | `'no-checkout'` | "`{repo}` is configured, but this machine has no cached checkout of it yet. Run any `intropy deploy` command once, then refresh." |
   | `'unreadable'` | `source.reason` verbatim (`LoadDeployConfig`'s message) |
   | `'ready'` + `!matched` | `matchReason` — *"…has not been onboarded to the GitOps repository"* or the ambiguity message with `candidates` listed |

   Only the fourth of these is about this integration. The first three are about the dashboard, and must never be phrased as if they were about the integration.

5. **Provenance footer**, always present when `state === 'ready'`: *"read from `{repo}` at `{revision.slice(0,7)}` (committed {age} ago), surveyed {age} ago"*, and when `!fetched`, *"not fetched from the remote — this is the checkout your last deploy command left behind."* Beside it a **"Refresh deployment state"** button, mirroring `.flow-refresh` in `FlowView.tsx:261` (state, disabled-while-pending, same class family).

`Sidebar.tsx` — **yes, a chip, but a narrow one.** Not a health dot: the sidebar has no room to be honest, and a red dot beside "not configured" is exactly the lie this design exists to avoid. So:

- `state === 'ready' && matched` → a small right-aligned chip with the release the **last** environment in promotion order runs (usually prod) — the single most-asked question — reusing the existing `.count` / `.chip-sub` styling.
- `consistent === false` → an additional `!` marker. This is a *positive* finding and is safe to render.
- **Anything else → nothing at all.** No chip is no claim. That rule is load-bearing.

1. **A third top-level view ("Deployments").** It rebuilds the same domain/system tree and splits "what is this integration" from "where is it running" — two halves of one question.
